ui_bugs.issue: React Native web strict-mode console error: 'Unexpected text node: . A text node cannot be a child of a <View>.' (4x on dashboard, 1x on schedule). Caused by stray whitespace/newline between JSX children directly inside a <View> — likely a template-literal or conditional-render whitespace leak. Non-blocking on web but will crash on native iOS/Android. Grep for View children with '{ ' or trailing whitespace in /app/frontend/app/(provider)/dashboard.tsx and /app/frontend/app/(provider)/schedule.tsx.

The 'Categories' section header renders on /(client)/home but NO category tiles/chips are drawn between it and 'Top rated' — the categories array is fetched (setCategories in useEffect) but only consumed by the Filters dropdown at line 363 of /app/frontend/app/(client)/home.tsx; nothing is rendered under the title at lines 229–231. Review request explicitly asked for 'categories with icons and provider cards'. Not a SDK-57 regression (same pattern in older iterations) but violates the review acceptance criterion.

action_items: MEDIUM — Track down the stray whitespace text node inside a <View> in the provider dashboard and schedule screens. On web this only logs an error; on native (iOS/Android) it will throw and crash the screen. Look for JSX like `<View>\n  {conditional && <X/>}\n  </View>` where a template literal or a bare space is being emitted as a child, and for `{something && ' '}`. Files to inspect: /app/frontend/app/(provider)/dashboard.tsx, /app/frontend/app/(provider)/schedule.tsx.

LOW — Decide whether the 'Categories' section on /(client)/home should render category chips/cards (with icons) or the section title should be removed. Currently the title is orphaned above the 'Top rated' section.

rca_of_issue: SDK 57 + Ionicons migration verified end-to-end. The one recurring React Native web warning ('Unexpected text node' inside a <View>) is a JSX child hygiene issue in the provider dashboard/schedule screen — stray whitespace/newline is being emitted as a text node directly under a <View>. This is a strict-mode error on native (New Architecture) and must be fixed before a device build, but does not break the web preview. Reproduction: log in as provider1@khedmapro.dz / password123 and open the dashboard — the error fires 4x. Mitigation: wrap any bare text/whitespace in <Text> or remove the leading/trailing whitespace between JSX children in the offending View.
